p_B is never defined in the receipt-bound statement text; the only definition on record ('p_B = sum over patterns mapped to B of Pr[pattern | B]') lives in the evidence file's "setting" field, and no definition from formulation p3-moment-bound-v1 is visible in this claim's record. A reader could take p_B as success probability conditioned on a conclusive outcome (renormalized), under which 'is at most 2/3' has different truth conditions. Likewise 'the dual-rail Bell pair' (singular) leaves implicit that p_B ranges over four distinct Bell-state inputs whose Fock encodings also appear only in "setting". [Statement phrase 'the average success (1/4) sum_B p_B' and 'acting on the dual-rail Bell pair' vs "setting" field of claims/evidence/p3_moment/k1_m6_p_avg_bound.json]

The identification of A_B(n) with the physical Born-rule amplitudes <n|out_B> (including multi-occupancy normalization for patterns with n_i >= 2) is a modeling bridge warranted only by package tests ('cross-validated against both float engines by tests/test_p3_poly_k1.py'); it sits outside both the machine_checked items and written_steps W0-W6, i.e., outside the disclosed verification boundary, yet the statement's p_B is a physical probability. [machine_checked (b) reference to 'bell_amp_poly (cross-validated against both float engines by tests/test_p3_poly_k1.py)' in claims/evidence/p3_moment/k1_m6_p_avg_bound.json]

Chain traced end-to-end against the statement: (I1) and (I2) at U^dag U = I give W1's D_i = Bell-basis matrix of Ohat_i; the statement's unambiguity clause gives W2 (Lambda_i Bell-diagonal, D_i - Lambda_i PSD); W3's transpose step is valid because D_i - Lambda_i is Hermitian PSD and Lambda_i real diagonal; W4 meets the dependency lemma's hypotheses (unit a, b; real s_A, s_B, c; u = 0 edge case handled; c_i = |U_i4|^2 >= 0); W5's three-photon count and W6's unit-column sums give 3*sum_B p_B <= 8, i.e., the stated 2/3, and min <= average yields the final clause; check (c) confirms the claimed bound is >= the proven (1+1)/(1+2). W0/W0' cover pure and mixed single-photon ancillas from the mode-5 case. No gap found between certificate-plus-written-steps and THIS statement.
